rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment inflicted on earlier deniers likewise befell these people; the Lord's word of punishment became binding on those who disbelieved, as promised for Iblis and his followers.
rows.anchor: { وكذلك } يعنى وهكذا عذبتهم، وكذلك { حقت كلمة ربك } يقول: وجبت كلمة العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bearers of the Throne are the first angels God created.
rows.anchor: وهم أول من خلق الله تعالى من الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels around the Throne are those surrounding it; Muqatil connects the angels' seeking forgiveness to Shura 42:5.
rows.anchor: فقال: { الذين يحملون العرش ومن حوله يسبحون بحمد ربهم } يقول: يذكرون الله بأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels glorify God by His command and affirm that He is one, without partner.
rows.anchor: يقول: يذكرون الله بأمره { ويؤمنون به } ويصدقون بالله عز وجل بأنه واحد لا شريك له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels' request for forgiveness is specifically for believers among earth's people.
rows.anchor: واختص استغفار الملائكة بالمؤمنين من أهل الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the angels' prayer, God's mercy is the blessing that creatures receive, and His knowledge encompasses the inhabitants of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: يعنى ملأت كل شىء من الحيوان فى السماوات والأرض { رحمة } يعنى نعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels ask forgiveness for those who repent of shirk, follow God's religion, and are protected from Hell.
rows.anchor: { فاغفر للذين تابوا } من الشرك { واتبعوا سبيلك } يعنى دينك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People emerge from their graves onto the earth, spread like a stretched hide, and none is hidden from God.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر ذلك اليوم، فقال: { يوم هم بارزون } من قبورهم على ظهر الأرض مثم الأديم الممدود { لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After taking the heavens and earth in His right hand, God asks who owns sovereignty; no one answers, so He answers that it belongs to God alone, without partner, who overpowers creatures when resurrecting them.
rows.anchor: حين قبض السموات والأرض فى يده اليمنى فلا يجيبه أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Resurrection, every righteous and wicked soul is repaid for good or evil with no injustice; God completes their reckoning in half a worldly day.
rows.anchor: { اليوم } فى الآخرة { تجزى كل نفس } بر وفاجر { بما كسبت } من خير أو شر { لا ظلم اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet warns Meccans of the approaching Hour, when those who see Hell gasp in terror and their hearts lodge in their throats and never return.
rows.anchor: الكفار إذا عاينوا النار فى الآخرة شخصت أبصارهم إليها فلا يطرفون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned are distressed polytheists with no helpful relative and no intercessor whose appeal is obeyed.
rows.anchor: { كاظمين } يعنى مكروبين { ما للظالمين } يعنى المشركين { من حميم } يعنى قريب ينفعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is the recompense of God's enemies, including Abu Jahl and his companions; they remain there because they denied Qur'anic signs despite knowing Muhammad was truthful.
rows.anchor: يعني أبا جهل وأصحابه، { لهم فيها دار الخلد } لا يموتون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement about those who distort God's signs was revealed concerning Abu Jahl ibn Hisham and Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: ونزل في أبي جهل بن هشام، وأبي بن خلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis was the first jinn to persist in sin; Adam's son who killed Abel was the first human to do so and the source of sin, whom the disbelievers want beneath their feet in Hell.
rows.anchor: لأنهما أول من أقاما على المعصية من الجن إبليس، ومن الإنس ابن آدم قاتل هابيل رأس الخطيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers knew that God is their Lord and remained steadfast in that knowledge without apostatizing; guardian angels descend in the afterlife to reassure them and promise the Garden.
rows.anchor: فعرفوه، { ثم استقاموا } على المعرفة، ولم يرتدوا عنها، { تتنزل عليهم الملائكة } في الآخرة من السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a believer leaves the grave, his recording angel identifies himself as the one who wrote the believer's good deeds; God had promised the Garden through messengers in worldly life.
rows.anchor: أنا الذي كنت أكتب عملك الصالح، فلا تخف ولا تحزن، وأبشر بالجنة التي كنت توعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God expanded provision for all His servants at once, they would rebel; instead He apportions it as He wills, knowing and seeing them. “In the earth” is fronted in the sentence.
rows.anchor: يعنى ولو وسع الله الرزق، { لعباده } ، فى ساعة واحدة، { لبغوا } ، يعنى لعصوا، { في الأرض } ، فيها تقديم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Meccans despaired during a seven-year withholding of rain, God sent rain and spread His blessing; He is believers' protector and praised by creation for the rain.
rows.anchor: المطر الذى حبس عنهم بمكة سبع سنين، { من بعد ما قنطوا } ، يعنى من بعد الإياسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs invite people to recognize God's oneness through His works though unseen; the creatures include angels in heaven and other beings on earth, whom God can gather at Resurrection.
rows.anchor: أن تعرفوا توحيد الرب وصنعه، وإن لم تروه، { خلق السماوات والأرض وما بث فيهما من دآبة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People cannot escape God through flight from their evil deeds and recompense; no close protector benefits them and no helper can prevent God.
rows.anchor: يعنى بسابقى الله هربا، { في الأرض } بأعمالكم الخبيثة حتى يجزيكم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ships sailing on the sea by wind resemble mountains on land and are signs of God's oneness through His works.
rows.anchor: يعنى السفن تجرى فى البحر بالرياح كالأعلام، شبه السفن فى البحر كالجبال فى البر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God stills the wind, ships remain stationary; their motion and stillness are lessons for the patient and thankful.
rows.anchor: قائمات على ظهر الماء، فلا تجرى، { إن في ذلك } الذى ترون، يعنى السفن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may destroy ships because of shirk, yet pardon many sins and save people from drowning; those disputing God's signs will learn they have no escape.
rows.anchor: يقول: وإن يشأ يهلكهن، يعنى السفن، { بما كسبوا } ، يعنى بما عملوا من الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Excuses will not benefit the polytheists who wronged themselves in worldly life; they and their devil companions share punishment.
rows.anchor: في الآخرة الاعتذار، { إذ ظلمتم } ، يقول: إذ أشركتم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deaf and blind are disbelievers unable to hear or see faith; the verse was revealed about an unnamed Meccan unbeliever clearly astray.
rows.anchor: { أفأنت تسمع الصم } الذين لا يسمعون الإيمان، يعني الكفار، { أو تهدي العمي }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God takes Muhammad in death, He will avenge Meccan unbelievers at Badr; alternatively, He may show Muhammad their promised punishment during his life, for He has power over them.
rows.anchor: قوله: { فإما نذهبن بك } ، يقول: فنميتك يا محمد، { فإنا منهم } ، يعني كفار مكة، { منتقمون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is to hold firmly to the Qur'an, for he follows a straight religion.
rows.anchor: { فاستمسك بالذي أوحي إليك } من القرآن، { إنك على صراط مستقيم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh, the Copt, called to his Coptic people and boasted that Egypt was his kingdom, forty by forty farsakhs, with rivers flowing below him; “do you not see?” means “why do you not?”
rows.anchor: قوله: { ونادى فرعون } القبطي، { في قومه } القبط، وكان نداؤه أنه { قال يقوم أليس لي ملك مصر } أربعين فرسخا في أربعين فرسخا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh challenges whether his people have gardens and rivers like his.
rows.anchor: { أفلا } ، يعني فهلا، { تبصرون } [آية: 51]، ألهم جنان وأنهار مثلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh claims he is better than Moses, whom he calls weak and lowly and unable to make his argument or speech clear; God had loosened Moses' tongue as recounted in Ta Ha 20:27 and 20:36.
rows.anchor: ثم قال فرعون: { أم أنآ خير } ، يقول: أنا خير، { من هذا } ، يعني موسى، { الذي هو مهين } ، يعني ضعيف ذليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh taunts that, if Moses were a truthful messenger, his Lord would have sent golden bracelets or angels to help his mission.
rows.anchor: { أسورة من ذهب } ، إن كان صادقا أنه رسول، { أو جآء معه الملائكة مقترنين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives life from sperm, causes death at appointed times, then gathers the first and last at Resurrection; most people do not know they will be raised, though resurrection is certain.
rows.anchor: { الله يحييكم } ، حين كانوا نطفة، { ثم يميتكم } عند أجالكم، { ثم يجمعكم إلى يوم القيامة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns the heavens and earth; when the Hour comes, those who deny resurrection lose.
rows.anchor: فقال: { ولله ملك السماوات والأرض ويوم تقوم الساعة } ، يعني يوم القيامة، { يومئذ يخسر المبطلون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every nation, meaning every soul, kneels for judgment, is summoned to its record of worldly good and evil, and is repaid for its deeds.
rows.anchor: { وترى كل أمة جاثية } على الركب عن الحساب، يعني كل نفس، { كل أمة تدعى إلى كتابها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine record speaks truthfully against people and was copied from the Preserved Tablet before they performed their deeds.
rows.anchor: { هذا كتابنا ينطق عليكم بالحق إنا كنا نستنسخ } من اللوح المحفوظ، { ما كنتم تعملون } [آية: 29] قبل أن تعملونها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says a copy can only be made from a book.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لا تكون نسخة إلا من كتاب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God admits believers who did righteous deeds into His mercy, meaning His Garden, and that entry is the clear triumph.
rows.anchor: { فأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فيدخلهم ربهم في رحمته } ، يعني في جنته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All praise means thanks belong to God, Lord of the heavens, earth, and all worlds; the phrase is associated with the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: قوله: { فلله الحمد } ، يقول: الشكر لله، { رب السماوت ورب الأرض رب العالمين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's grandeur means greatness, sovereignty, strength, and power throughout the heavens and earth; He is mighty in His kingdom and wise in His command.
rows.anchor: يعني العظمة، والسلطان، والقوة، والقدرة في السموات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to treat parents well was revealed about Abu Bakr, son of Abu Quhafa; his mother was Umm al-Khayr bint Sakhr.
rows.anchor: يعني برا بهم نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق، رضي الله عنه، ابن أبي قحافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mother bears and delivers her child with hardship; pregnancy lasts nine months and weaning twenty-one, totaling thirty months. Maturity is eighteen years, and strength lasts until forty.
rows.anchor: يعني حملته في مشقة ووضعته في مشقة { وحمله } في البطن تسعة أشهر { وفصاله } من اللبن واحدا وعشرين شهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr believed the Prophet at forty; asking for inspiration to gratitude means thanking God for Islam given to him and his parents.
rows.anchor: فلما بلغ أبو بكر أربعين سنة، صدق بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr asks to do pleasing righteous deeds and for all his children to become believers; the source links this to 40:8.
rows.anchor: ثم قال: { و } ألهمنى { وأن أعمل صالحا ترضاه وأصلح لي في ذريتي } يقول واجعل أولادي مؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr repents from shirk and calls himself one of those sincere in monotheism.
rows.anchor: ثم قال أبو بكر: { إني تبت إليك } من الشرك { وإني من المسلمين } [آية: 15] يعني من المخلصين بالتوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people addressed are Jewish hypocrites; turning away would mean corrupting the land through sins and severing family ties.
rows.anchor: { فهل عسيتم } يعني منافقي اليهود { إن توليتم أن تفسدوا في الأرض } بالمعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened severing of ties refers to kinship between those Jews and the Ansar.
rows.anchor: قال: وكان بينهم وبين الأنصار قرابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The manifest victory is Hudaybiyyah; after Muhammad returned, God revealed the verse in Medina, and “victory” means that God decreed Islam for him.
rows.anchor: { إنا فتحنا لك } يوم الحديبية { فتحا مبينا } [آية: 1] وذلك أن الله تعالى أنزل بمكة على نبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccan polytheists mocked Muhammad's earlier statement that he did not know what would be done to him or them, arguing a genuine messenger would know the future as Solomon and Jesus' disciples did.
rows.anchor: ومآ أدري ما يفعل بي ولا بكم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: After Abu Bakr and Umar asked what God would do to him, Muhammad replied that God had not yet brought him any new matter.
rows.anchor:
للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: ألا تخبرنا ما الله فاعل بك؟ فقال:
" ما أحدث الله إلى أمر بعد "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the return from Hudaybiyyah, Ibn Ubayy, chief of the hypocrites, mocked believers for following a man who did not know what God would do to him or his followers.
rows.anchor: قال عبدالله بن أبي رأس المنافقين: كيف تتعبون رجلا لا يدري ما يفعل الله به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knew believers' sadness and the joy of Meccan polytheists and Medinan hypocrites, then revealed the verse in Medina after Hudaybiyyah.
rows.anchor: وعلم الله ما في قلوب المؤمنين من الحزن، وعلم فرح المشركين من أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “So that He may forgive you” means God forgives Muhammad's earlier sin from the pre-Islamic period and what followed after his prophethood.
rows.anchor: { ليغفر } يعني لكي يغفر { لك الله } الإسلام { ما تقدم من ذنبك } يعني ما كان في الجاهلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God completes His blessing upon Muhammad and guides him to a straight path, meaning a straight religion.
rows.anchor: { ويتم نعمته عليك ويهديك صراطا مستقيما } [آية: 2] يعني دينا مستقيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scattering winds are winds that scatter dust.
rows.anchor: { والذاريات ذروا } [آية: 1] يعني الرياح ذرت ذروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The laden bearers are clouds heavy with water, while the smooth-moving ones are ships passing swiftly.
rows.anchor: { فالحاملات وقرا } [آية: 2] يعني السحاب موقرة من الماء { فالجاريات يسرا } [آية: 3] يعني السفن مرت مرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distributors of command are four angels—Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, and the Angel of Death—who administer matters among creatures by God's command.
rows.anchor: أربعة من الملائكة جبريل، وميكائيل، وإسرافيل، وملك الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears by these signs that the promised Hour is true and reckoning will certainly occur.
rows.anchor: فأقسم الله تعالى، بهؤلاء الآيات { إنما توعدون } يعني إن الذي توعدون من أمر الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad's sight did not swerve or transgress; he did not wrong what he saw that night.
rows.anchor: { ما زاغ البصر } يعني بصر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم يعني ما مال { وما طغى } [آية: 17] يعني وما ظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad truly saw God's great signs: a green coverlet covered the horizon.
rows.anchor: رأى رفرفا أخضر قد غطى الأفق، فذلك من آيات ربه الكبرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Lat and al-Uzza's names arose when people wanted to name idols after Allah and al-Aziz, but God prevented this and the names changed.
rows.anchor: وإنما سميت اللات والعزى لأنهم أرادوا أن يسموا الله، فمنعهم الله فصارت اللات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because they claimed angels were God's daughters, the passage rebukes them for reserving sons for themselves and assigning God daughters, an unjust division.
rows.anchor: { ألكم الذكر وله الأنثى } [آية: 21] حين قالوا: إن الملائكة بنات الله { تلك إذا قسمة ضيزى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols are names invented by people and their ancestors without revealed proof; authority means a book containing evidence, as in 37:156 and 30:35.
rows.anchor: { إن هي } يقول: ما هي { إلا أسمآء سميتموهآ أنتم وآبآؤكم مآ أنزل الله بها من سلطان } بأنها آلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idolaters follow conjecture and desire rather than knowledge that al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat are gods; the guidance sent by their Lord is the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: يقول: ما لهم من علم بأنها آلهة إلا ظنا ما يستيقنون بأن اللات والعزى ومناة آلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their wish that angels intercede for them is what the question about whether a person gets what he wishes addresses.
rows.anchor: بأن الملائكة تشفع لهم، وذلك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ سورة النجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: During a public recitation of Surat al-Najm, Satan put a phrase praising the exalted cranes and hoped-for intercession on Muhammad's tongue; Meccan polytheists rejoiced and hoped for angelic intercession.
rows.anchor: نعس فألقى الشيطان على لسانه تلك " الثالثة الأخرى تلك الغرانيق العلا " عندها الشفاعة ترتجى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the surah's end, Muhammad and the believers prostrated in affirmation of God, while Meccan polytheists prostrated at the idols; the elderly Walid ibn al-Mughira prostrated by lifting dirt to his forehead.
rows.anchor: فلما بلغ أخرها سجد، وسجد المؤمنون تصديقا لله تعالى وسجد كفار مكة عند ذكر الآهلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After people hoped that angels would intercede, God declared that both the afterlife and this world belong to Him; the author links this to resurrection and recompense.
rows.anchor: فلما رجوا أن الملائكة شفاعة، أنزل الله تعالى: { فلله الآخرة والأولى } [آية: 25] يعني الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Meccan polytheists were told to prostrate to al-Rahman, they denied knowing that name; God identifies Himself and recounts His works so people may know and worship Him alone.
rows.anchor: فأكروا الرحمن، وقالوا: لا نعرف الرحمن، فأخبر الله تعالى عن نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The al-Rahman whom they denied taught the Qur'an, created Adam, and taught him speech—the explanation of all things.
rows.anchor: فقال: { الرحمن } الذي أنكروه هو الذي { علم القرآن خلق الإنسان } [آية: 3] يعني آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Garden's women were created in the Garden and were not touched by any human or jinn before its people.
rows.anchor: لأنهن خلقن في الجنة، يعني لم يطأهن إنس قبل أهل الجنة، ولا جان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Green rafraf means cushions above the beds, and fine abqari means beautiful carpets of velvet.
rows.anchor: يعني المحابس فوق الفرش { وعبقري حسان } [آية: 76] يعني الزرابي، وهي الطنافس المخملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord's name is blessed; majesty means greatness and honor means generosity—none is more generous—and God praises Himself.
rows.anchor: { فبأي آلاء ربكما تكذبان تبارك اسم ربك ذي الجلال } يعني بالجلال والعظيم { والإكرام } [آية: 78] يعني الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul reaching the throat means it reaches the collarbones.
rows.anchor: ثم وعظهم فقال: { فلولا } يعني فهلا { إذا بلغت } هذه النفس { الحلقوم } [آية: 83] يعني التراقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those present witness God's command and power; closer means the Angel of Death alone, who comes to take the soul, though they cannot see him.
rows.anchor: { وأنتم حينئذ تنظرون } [آية: 84] إلى أمرى وسلطانى { ونحن أقرب إليه منكم } يعني ملك الموت وحده إذ أتاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not being accountable means not subject to reckoning; the source compares other verses about the Day of Judgment and challenges people to return the soul if truthful.
rows.anchor: { إن كنتم غير مدينين } [آية: 86] يعنيغير محاسبين، نظيرها في فاتحة الكتاب ملك يوم الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For one among those brought near, rest means relief, fragrant provision means provision in the Garden, and he receives Gardens of bliss.
rows.anchor: يعني ما كان فيه لشدة الموت وكربه { فروح } يعني فراحه { وريحان } يعني الرزق في الجنة بلسان خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is one: the unseen is what has been and will be, and the witnessed is His truthful testimony in every matter.
rows.anchor: فقال: { هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو عالم الغيب } يعني غيب ما كان وما يكون { والشهادة } يعني شهادته بالحق فى كل شىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rahman and al-Rahim are two gentle names, one gentler than the other; Arab polytheists said they knew only the name Allah.
rows.anchor: اسمان رقيقان، أحدهما أرق من الآخر، فلما ذكر { الرحمن الرحيم } ، قال مشركو العرب: ما نعرف الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition concerns Jews and was revealed about Abdullah ibn Ubayy and Malik ibn Dakhsham, whom Jews urged to leave Islam; poor Muslims shared news with Jews to receive their fruit and food, so God forbade this.
rows.anchor: يعني اليهود نزلت في عبد الله بن أبي، ومالك بن دخشم كانت اليهود زينوا لهم ترك الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews' despair of the afterlife is likened to a dead unbeliever's despair after an angel shows him Hell and the dwelling in Paradise he forfeited; he realizes he has no share in its good.
rows.anchor: فلو كنت آمنت بربك لدخلت الجنة، ثم فينظر إليها، فيقول: لمن هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created seven heavens in two days, each layered above the next; the distance between heavens and the thickness of each are each five hundred years' travel.
rows.anchor: { الذي خلق سبع سماوات } في يومين { طباقا } بعضها فوق بعض بين كل سماءين مسيرة خمسمائة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No disparity means no defect in the heavens; looking again means repeating one's gaze, and fissures means gaps or openings.
rows.anchor: يقول ماترى ابن آدم في خلق السموات من عيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On looking twice, sight returns humbled; strained sight gathers water, and weary means worn out and unable to find a flaw or opening.
rows.anchor: يعني إذا اشتد البصر يقع فيه الماء، خاسئا: يعني صاغرا { وهو حسير } [آية: 4]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth was made submissive by being fixed with mountains so it would not shift; people may travel safely through its regions as they wish.
rows.anchor: أثبتها بالجبال لئلا تزول بأهلها { فامشوا } يعني فمروا { في مناكبها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are told to eat from God's lawful provision.
rows.anchor: { وكلوا من رزقه } الحلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final gathering is returning to God alive from the graves after death.
rows.anchor: يقول: إلى الله تعبثون من قبوركم أحياء بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier nations denied messengers and were punished; “how was My rejection?” means God's punishment and repudiation, warning Meccan unbelievers to learn and affirm God's oneness.
rows.anchor: يعني قبل كفار مكة من الأمم الخالية رسلهم فعذبناهم { فكيف كان نكير } [آية: 18] يعني تغييري وإنكاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birds spread and fold their wings above people; only al-Rahman sustains them through both motions, and He sees all His creation.
rows.anchor: الأجنحة حين يردن أن يعن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No party can protect Meccans from God's punishment, and no other god can provide rain if God withholds it; He alone provides, yet they persist in arrogant disbelief and turn from faith.
rows.anchor: يقول الله تعالى: أنا الرزاق، قال: { بل لجوا في عتو } يعني تمادوا في الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Jahl, the disbeliever, walks astray, fallen on his face and blind in heart; Muhammad walks upright as a believer on Islam's straight path with a pure heart.
rows.anchor: يعني الكافر يمشي ضالا في الكفر أعمى القلب، يعني أبا جهل بن هشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The harsh man is big-bellied, constricted in the throat, gluttonous, given to drinking, violent, and unjust; zanīm is an extra growth on his ear like a sheep's wattle.
rows.anchor: يعني بالعتل رحيب الجوف موثق الحلق، أكول شروب غشوم ظلوم، ومعنى { زنيم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about having wealth and sons refers to al-Walid.
rows.anchor: { أن كان } يعني إذا كان { ذا مال وبنين } [آية: 14] { إذا تتلى عليه } يعني الوليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Walid called the Qur'an tales of the ancients, meaning false stories such as those of Rustam and Asfandbaz.
rows.anchor: يقول: أحاديث الأولين وكذبهم وهو حديث رستم واسفندباز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God marks al-Walid's nose black; before Hell his face turns black, eyes blue, face downward, and he is shackled in iron.
rows.anchor: يعني على الأنف، وهو الوليد، وذلك أنه يسود وجهه وتزرق عيناه
